ai.description: This slender lizard reaches 30 cm, mostly tail. It is brown with two distinct white or yellow lateral stripes. It features keeled dorsal scales and long, whip-like toes for climbing grass.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue is the presence of three distinct, bright white or yellow longitudinal stripes running along each side of its slender, extremely long tail and body.
ai.habitat: The Asian Grass Lizard inhabits open grasslands, scrublands, and forest edges, typically found in low-to-mid altitudes ranging from sea level up to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Asian Grass Lizard is a diurnal forager that uses its long, prehensile tail to navigate through tall grasses while actively hunting small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Takydromus sexlineatus* is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 1–5 eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, peaking during the monsoon season in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Takydromus sexlineatus* occurs in Northeast India, primarily in Assam and surrounding states, inhabiting low-to-mid elevation grasslands and forest edges.
